question: Should OpenClaw commit to official FreeBSD support, and if so at what support tier and owner boundary?
rationale: The request spans release distribution, platform support policy, service management, CI capacity, docs, and ongoing package ownership, which cannot be safely chosen by an automated fix lane.

options.title: Keep Open For Owner-Backed Plan
options.body: Keep this issue as the product decision point until a maintainer or owner commits to the FreeBSD support tier, packaging owner, and release-validation scope.

options.title: Narrow To Community Package
options.body: Accept only a community-maintained FreeBSD ports/pkg path without calling it Tier 1 support, and require docs to state the support boundary clearly.

options.title: Decline Tier 1 For Now
options.body: Close or mark not planned if maintainers do not want to own FreeBSD release validation and platform support yet.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Owner-Backed Plan
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the product decision point until a maintainer or owner commits to the FreeBSD support tier, packaging owner, and release-validation scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad support decision crosses installer, service lifecycle, docs, and release surfaces where recent history points to Peter Steinberger as the strongest routing candidate.
